footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$560K in 2025). From pre-tax income to net loss: includes a $16.8M income tax benefit. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) fell 58.2% to $29.4M in 2025. Net interest income rose 15.8% to $106M and noninterest income was −$76.7M, versus −$21.4M; noninterest expense rose 3.3%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net loss was −$35.7M, versus −$8.4M, or −$2.24 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 276.7% versus 112.1%. Bank of Marin Bancorp returned $16.1M through dividends.
